papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable self‐powered sensors capable of monitoring multiple physiological signals are highly desirable for next‐generation healthcare electronics, yet achieving decoupled multi‐signal sensing within a single compact system remains challenging. Here, we report a self‐powered, rechargeable multimodal soft sensor (SRMS sensor) based on a multilayered zinc‐air battery design for decoupled O 2 and temperature monitoring. The SRMS sensor utilizes a potassium polyacrylate/polyacrylamide hydrogel as the polyelectrolyte, and employs a Co 3 O 4 /graphene‐coated nickel foam cathode for O 2 concentration monitoring, as well as a Zn‐electrodeposited graphite film anode for temperature sensing. It is demonstrated that the sensor can be used for contactless temperature‐sensing, thermal imaging, and information input through sensor‐array integration. During the respiratory gas monitoring, the SRMS sensor shows decoupled negative and positive responses of relative current change upon O 2 and temperature stimuli. The SRMS sensor also successfully distinguishes different respiratory states, identifies sleep‐related respiratory disturbance events, and monitors skin‐temperature variations during sleep. This work provides a novel strategy for constructing multimodal self‐powered soft sensors with decoupled sensing capability, which shows promising applications in wearable healthcare monitoring and contactless information interaction.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Noninvasive wearable sweat sensors are promising for personalized health management, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by complex multi‐component architectures, reliance on rigid batteries, and a lack of intuitive visual feedback. Herein, we propose a sweat‐powered metabolism‐to‐visual transduction mechanism that utilizes sweat as both an energy source and a detection target. A fabric‐based sweat electricity harvester is fabricated, which harnesses sweat energy to yield a stable power output, enabling battery‐free sensing operation. Coupled enzymatic sensing electrode–electrochromic display system translates sweat glucose concentration into directly perceptible color change. To overcome the subjective errors inherent in traditional colorimetry, a neural network‐based smartphone application is employed to provide precise quantitative visual readouts, achieving highly accurate estimation of sweat glucose (R 2 = 0.997) comparable to commercial assay kits in on‐body evaluation on human subjects. By successfully decoupling wearable sensors from rigid power sources while fusing self‐powered electrochromic displays with AI‐assisted digital readouts, this lightweight textile platform establishes an on‐demand strategy for user‐friendly, and intelligent metabolic monitoring.

papers.source_abstract: Tactile sensing is essential for robots to interact effectively with humans, objects, and their environment. While soft tactile fingers have emerged to emulate human touch, existing designs often fall short in perceiving subtle material features, struggle with textures on deformable surfaces, and treat softness and texture recognition as separate tasks. Here, we present a tendon‐driven soft robotic finger with a multimodal tactile fingertip capable of simultaneously discerning texture and softness through automated human‐like finger motion. The finger integrates a compliant, anthropomorphic structure with a multimodal fingertip embedding pressure, accelerometer, and gyroscope sensors within a soft elastomer. As the finger slides over materials, a hybrid CNN‐LSTM deep learning pipeline processes multimodal tactile cues to classify material properties. Extensive experiments demonstrate classification of 18 textures with 94.3% accuracy and four softness levels with 97.9% accuracy. In combined texture‐softness tests across 20 samples, the system achieved 95.4% accuracy for texture and 97.0% for softness recognition. These results highlight the finger’s ability to perceive complex material properties that prior soft tactile fingers failed to resolve. By bridging the gap between human‐like perception and soft tactile sensing, the proposed system advances capabilities for adaptive grasping, refined object manipulation, material sorting, and prosthetic applications.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Global energy demand has rapidly increased for sustainable and self‐powered wearable electronic devices. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have emerged as a promising approach for generating electrical energy by harvesting mechanical energy from daily human activities. In this report, magnesium oxide (MgO (MO)) nanoparticles (NPs) were prepared via a one‐step hydrothermal method. Subsequently, various concentrations of MO NPs were incorporated into poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP), and nanofiber films (NFs) were fabricated via an electrospinning process. The fabricated films displayed high flexibility, making them suitable for motion‐induced sensing and energy harvesting applications. Furthermore, the maximum electrical output performance was achieved with 0.05 wt% MO/PVDF‐HFP NF. The optimized MO/PVDF‐HFP NF‐based TENG exhibited a voltage, current, charge density, and power density of 180 V, 5 µA, 45 µCm −2 , and 1.5 Wm −2 , respectively. The TENG was further evaluated for device robustness, stability, and long‐term durability. Furthermore, the TENG was integrated into a self‐powered boundary‐detection security system that can detect human movement in restricted or unauthorized areas. This approach can pave the way to advance self‐powered security and boundary‐monitoring systems by providing a sustainable, low‐cost, and energy‐efficient strategy for autonomous security technologies.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid metal particles‐silicone composite ink has garnered significant attention in the field of stretchable electronics due to its exceptional conductivity and deformability. However, traditional platinum‐catalyzed addition‐cure liquid silicone rubber‐based conductive ink suffers from an extremely short pot life at room temperature, which leads to premature crosslinking, nozzle jamming, and material waste during the printing process. To address this challenge, this study introduces a liquid multiple vinyl siloxane (PC‐611) as an inhibitor of the hydrosilylation reaction, which can form a reversible chelation with the platinum catalyst, successfully extending the room‐temperature pot life to over 10 days while enabling rapid curing at 100°C when above 2 wt.% PC‐611 content. Furthermore, the composite ink exhibits excellent shear‐thinning rheological properties even after being stored for ten days, making it highly compatible with direct ink writing (DIW). The printed flexible circuits demonstrate robust electromechanical stability and show a resistance change ratio of less than 0.4 under 30% strain. The composite ink formulation proposed herein effectively resolves the ink storage and process stability challenge during the manufacturing process of stretchable circuits, and offers a reliable solution for the large‐scale fabrication of silicone‐based stretchable electronic devices.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite single crystal arrays combine the advantages of low defect density, coherent lattice orientation and multiplexed channels, which offer great potential across various fields ranging from energy conversion and signal detection to flexible electronics. However, the poor regularity in the morphology, composition, and heterophase of perovskite arrays poses a major challenge in manipulating the optical and electronic characteristics. Here, we demonstrate a non‐invasive general epitaxial growth approach for fabricating perovskite single‐crystalline heterostructure arrays with programmable dimensions, geometry, and composition on various substrates. The solvation structure during array epitaxy is meticulously manipulated by co‐solvents, which minimizes the detrimental nucleus dissolution and favors the formation of well‐defined and uniform perovskite heterostructure arrays. The electronic properties of the fabricated perovskite arrays approach those of bulk single crystals with a carrier mobility of 18.29 cm 2 V – 1 s −1 and a trap density of 5.76 × 10 12 cm −3 . Using these heterostructure arrays, micro‐LED devices have been fabricated exhibiting unique electrochromic function. The programmable production of perovskite heterostructure arrays offers a well‐defined platform for fundamental studies and device integration of perovskite‐based optoelectronics.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochromic materials, which enable reversible modulation of transmittance, absorbance, and reflectance across the UV–Vis‐NIR spectrum, are classic examples of active optical materials. While the field of electrochromism has witnessed explosive growth in multimetal systems over the past two decades, the literature remains fragmented across materials chemistry, solid‐state physics, and device engineering. This review provides the first systematic roadmap of the evolution from single‐metal to multimetal‐based electrochromic materials, addressing a critical gap in the literature across materials chemistry, solid‐state physics, and device engineering. We establish a detailed structure–property–performance framework for transparent conducting electrodes (TCEs), anodic, cathodic, and electrolyte materials, while critically evaluating performance parameters and identifying inconsistencies in reporting to propose standardized protocols. Furthermore, we assess cutting‐edge multifunctional integrations, including electrochromic energy storage, batteries, self‐powered systems, flexible electronics, and thermochromic hybrids, revealing how multimetal designs enhance optical, electrochemical, and mechanical properties. Concluding with a forward‐looking roadmap, we outline four actionable challenges: rational materials discovery via machine learning, metal's criticality and Safe‐and‐Sustainable‐by‐Design, operando interfacial engineering, sustainable fabrication, and IoT integration. This authoritative reference bridges fundamental insights with device‐level performance, accelerating next‐generation electrochromic systems for smart windows, wearable displays, building decarbonization, and intelligent infrastructure.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Soft bioelectronics require conductive hydrogels with balanced mechanical–electrical performance for high‐fidelity electrophysiological recording, yet conventional ones lack a balance between stretchability and electrochemical stability due to poor interfacial charge transfer. We present a molecularly engineered polyoxometalate‐functionalized mesoporous metal–organic framework (meso‐MOF@POM) nanoarchitecture that simultaneously reinforces the hydrogel network and enhances interfacial charge kinetics. The meso‐MOF serves as a hierarchical scaffold with multiscale channels for polymer anchoring, while the sub‐nanometer Keggin‐type POM layer creates abundant redox‐mediated electron transfer pathways. Upon integration of meso‐MOF@POM into a dual‐network poly(acrylic acid)/polyacrylamide hydrogel, the composite hydrogel enables high stretchability (>1000% strain), minimal electrical creep ( −1 @100% strain), and good cyclic durability (>3000 cycles). Crucially, the engineered organic–inorganic interface endows the hydrogel with excellent pseudocapacitive charge‐transfer kinetics, which achieves low skin–electrode impedance (64 kΩ at 1 Hz vs. 287 kΩ at 1 Hz for Ag/AgCl gel). As a result, the skin‐interfacing electrode enables high‐fidelity recording of on‐skin electrophysiological signals, including electrocardiogram, electromyogram, and electrooculogram, with an enhanced signal‐to‐noise ratio (e.g., 23.8 dB for ECG vs. 21.3 dB for Ag/AgCl gel). This work provides a novel fabrication strategy for highly conductive interfaces, enabling long‐term applications in wearable health monitors and human–machine interfaces.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Surface metallization of polyimide (PI) films is essential for constructing conductive electrodes and interconnects in flexible electronics, directly determining device integration and reliability. However, the high inertness and low surface energy of PI necessitate complex pretreatment in conventional vacuum deposition, incurring high costs and substrate damage, while wet etching faces environmental burdens and poor compatibility, both failing to meet large‐scale manufacturing demands. Inspired by the stable coordination of histidine in Nereis jaws, a coordination‐directed molecular design strategy is proposed. By introducing nitrogen‐containing heterocyclic units into PI molecular chains, intrinsic metal anchoring sites are constructed, enabling direct film metallization without destructive adhesion‐promoting surface pretreatments. This process integrates with photolithography, printing, and direct writing for cross‐scale controllable metallization, fabricating planar wiring and vertical interconnect access (VIA) structures for 3D high‐density integration. The metallized PI films with azaindole‐bearing diamine moieties achieve the highest 5B‐grade adhesion and exhibit excellent environmental stability, tolerating repeated bending, high‐temperature exposure, and ultrasonic impact. Commercial PI surface metallization can be achieved with minimal functional monomers and is directly compatible with electronic soldering and device integration. This strategy overcomes the trade‐off between interfacial adhesion and substrate integrity, providing a viable pathway for scalable flexible electronics manufacturing.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible wearable electronics in the 5G/6G era require multifunctional fabrics integrating electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, sensing, electro‐thermal conversion, and thermal insulation, yet these properties are inherently incompatible. Herein, we modified the surface of a 2D network in non‐woven fabric (NWF) by doping Cl– into PPy (NWF‐P‐X) through a simple controllable layer‐by‐layer immersing–polymerization process. The introduction of Cl – ‐doped PPy shell constructed conductive networks within 2D NWF matrices, resulting in boosted electrical conductivity ( σ ) (65.13 S/m), electro‐thermal conversion efficiency, and pressure‐responsive sensing performance. The high σ endowed the NWF‐P‐X with great wide‐frequency absorption‐dominated EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE). The SET was beyond 25 dB (99.68377% shielding capacity) over 30 MHz–4.5 GHz and beyond 40 dB (99.99% shielding) over 8.0–40.0 GHz. The NWF‐P‐X also presented a rapid heat response under a low voltage (4.0 V) and a wide temperature range (29.6°C–107.4°C). Moreover, the NWF‐P‐X exhibited superior thermal insulation performance with low thermal conductivity (0.5537 W∙m −1 ∙K −1 in‐plane; 0.0650 W∙m −1 ∙K −1 out‐of‐plane), where the porous structure and phase interfaces critically enable multifunctional compatibility for EMI protection, thermal management, and sensing applications.
